title: Iridescent Material Transfer Workshop
description: A split-screen material workshop where the IridescenceAbalone shell serves as a source of exotic material properties and the Corset serves as the target garment. The user extracts material channels (iridescence, roughness, metalness, color, emissive, normal intensity) from the shell, mixes them in a central blending node, and applies the composite material to the corset — with a total energy budget that conserves across all channels, full undo/redo support, and coupled slider interactions.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 with GLTFLoader and OrbitControls from CDN. Load IridescenceAbalone.glb on the left and Corset.glb on the right, both on a dark studio backdrop with three-point lighting (key, fill, rim) plus an HDR-style environment map using PMREMGenerator with a procedural gradient. Camera starts at z=3 looking at center. Build an HTML overlay UI panel in the center with six vertical sliders: Iridescence Intensity, Roughness, Metalness, Base Color Hue, Emissive Glow, and Normal Strength. Implement a conservation law: all six sliders share a total energy budget of 3.0 units (each slider ranges 0-1). When any slider increases, the others must proportionally decrease to maintain the sum, creating multi-input coupling. Display the remaining budget numerically. Add a Transfer button that applies the current slider mix to the Corset's MeshPhysicalMaterial properties in real time — iridescence and iridescenceIOR map from slider 1, roughness from slider 2, metalness from slider 3, color hue-shift from slider 4, emissiveIntensity from slider 5, and normalScale from slider 6. The abalone shell should visually dim on the transferred channels (reduce its own values inversely) to show energy leaving the source. Implement an undo/redo stack (at least 15 states) triggered by keyboard Z/Y or on-screen buttons, storing full slider snapshots. Add a Randomize button that picks a valid budget-respecting configuration. Add a Reset button restoring defaults. The user must: adjust at least 4 sliders, transfer twice, undo at least once, redo once, randomize once, reset once, re-transfer, and rotate both models via OrbitControls — totaling 10-14 interaction steps for a complete workflow. Animate the corset with a slow Y-rotation. Show a step counter tracking completed interaction milestones out of 12.
